newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Mexico sees growth despite trade, rate concerns.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sees growth despite trade, rate concerns.

text.p: Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said on Sunday the Mexican economy is likely to weather the threats of rising interest rates and a widening current account deficit.
"The fundamentals of the Mexican economy...are on track," Ortiz told Reuters Financial Television.

He said the recent hike in United States short-term interest rates would have a short-term effect on the domestic rate, "but again the underlying inflation which continues to go down will underpin lower domestic rates".
He said the Mexican stock market had in fact weathered the recent rate hike.
Ortiz said he expected the country's gross domestic product to reach 4.5 percent.
He added that it would be inevitable that imports would outpace exports in the coming months.

"We are projecting for this year a current account deficit of less than 2.0 percent of GDP ... There is no cause for concern, because direct foreign investment will certainly be more than enough to finance this type of current account deficit," he added.
